<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf993619cdf3f733d470683e3f89e75fd643f01f` — the merge of head `b77896a251cdea32aa08d83f57e399154f3a5d45` into base `f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf993619cdf3f733d470683e3f89e75fd643f01f && git checkout cf993619cdf3f733d470683e3f89e75fd643f01f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9 b77896a251cdea32aa08d83f57e399154f3a5d45 && git checkout -B drift-repro f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9 && git merge --no-ff b77896a251cdea32aa08d83f57e399154f3a5d45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 385ed2b4 · 2026-11-24T03:20Z

Head-sha: `385ed2b4289f383c2aca40539486f422b49fcd27`
Card: #36400 · os-dev-report 7120437180 (area ux-D).

### Checklist
- **Shape:** `l1-face` at this head. Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36400`, no closing keyword next to another card.
  - The card's premise ("object-embedded / app-bundled flows") is refuted in the PR: `object.zod.ts` and `app.zod.ts` carry no embedded flow list. The PR records this in public, so the correction is on the record.
  - Step 2 of the card (widen to every declared flow a reader draws, in the same change as the reader it relies on) is delivered against the reader that exists: the docs viewer's `type: flow` embed titles its card `translated?.flowLabel ?? flow.label ?? …`, read on `main` at `ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx:556-571`, for any flow a page names.
  - Step 3 (re-baseline and say the rise) is delivered.

  `Fixes` is right.
- **Checks at this head:** 68 check-runs. 57 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check: success. The coverage ratchet is green on the raised baseline. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Governance:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36826`: NOT governed, 138 lines.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. No `packages/spec` file is in the diff and no export moves, so no contract face and no L2 is owed. The lint demand widens for authors, which is a lint finding, not an accept set; the changeset states it.
- **Rule change:** `walkScreenFlows` pushes `flows.<flow>.label` for every named flow (a nameless flow is skipped earlier). The docblock is rewritten to name the three readers and to keep the walk's own rule ("a string nobody reads is not demanded"). `hasScreen` is still read by the toast branch below.
- **Tests:**
  - The five narrow-predicate pins are flipped. The rewritten pins add a seeded-label check, a nameless-flow check, and a "goes quiet once translated" control in one tree.
  - Lint whole suite: 229 files, 9513 tests. The ablation restored the old predicate through dist and got 5 red.
- **Baseline:** `app-showcase` 425 → 449 and `app-todo` 130 → 136, exactly the new findings; the changeset says the same. The other twelve configs are unchanged.
- **Changeset prose, read sentence by sentence:**
  - every named flow now asked: true;
  - the two former readers: true;
  - the docs embed titles any flow by the key: true (as read above);
  - what you see after upgrading: one more `i18n/missing-flow` per untranslated locale per such flow, and `os i18n extract` scaffolds it: consistent with the walker feeding extract and the coverage check;
  - nameless flow not asked: true, pinned;
  - the ratchet numbers: match.

### Findings
- **S1 (should-fix)** — `@objectstack/cli` is touched and has no changeset entry; `l1-face` flags it.
  - `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts` changes, a comment line only.
  - The package is published (`files: ["dist", …]`) and builds with `tsc`, which keeps comments, so the shipped `dist/utils/i18n-coverage.js` changes too.
  - More to the point, the user-visible change lands in the CLI's own commands: `os lint`, `os i18n check` and `os i18n extract`, which the changeset itself names.
  - l1-review-checklist: every touched package with `private: false` is published, so check its changeset; "⛔ 判据不是改动大小 … ⛔ 缺了不入队".
  - Fix: add `'@objectstack/cli': patch` to `.changeset/36400-flow-label-every-flow.md`. No other change. A delta read on the new head follows at once.

Must-fix: none. No nits.

### Next
Push the one-line changeset fix. I re-read on the new head (delta: changeset only) and give ACCEPT if nothing else moved.
